title: Mempool Surf Club Explore — Ordinals Research Registry
scope: Research-only registry section for the ORDINALS category. This file does not publish or activate Explore content.

source_of_truth.rule: The manifest plus all listed record shards together are the canonical machine-readable source. Command Center review is required before promotion to a Master Explore Registry.

registry_wide_rules.one_entity_one_profile: One canonical profile per entity; child releases, tokens, and cross-category assets should be represented as relationships unless the Master Explore Registry explicitly requires a separate canonical entity.
registry_wide_rules.status_rule: ACTIVE requires verified current project/protocol/community operation; HISTORICAL means finite/completed or chiefly historical; INACTIVE means project operation has ceased or creator has explicitly stepped away; UNCERTAIN means current status or core attribution cannot be verified confidently.
registry_wide_rules.protocol_rule: Distinguish Bitcoin consensus rules from application-layer conventions, indexer-derived state, metaprotocol rules, and project claims.
registry_wide_rules.publication_rule: Recommended slugs and descriptions are planning data only. No Shopify page, Atlas widget, template, runtime file, public card, or production route is created by this registry.
registry_wide_rules.source_rule: Prefer official project/docs/GitHub/social sources, then on-chain/indexers/reputable marketplaces, then independent coverage. Marketplace listings alone are not sufficient for a fully verified profile.
registry_wide_rules.cross_category_rule: Entities whose canonical home is another Explore category are linked, not duplicated. Examples: DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON and RSIC•GENESIS•RUNE belong in RUNES.

topic_architecture.purpose: Standards, protocols, indexing conventions, and experiments that use Ordinals inscriptions or ordinal-aware infrastructure as a substrate.
Canonical art, PFP, community, conceptual, generative, recursive, rare-sat, and distribution projects whose identity is materially tied to Ordinals.
Historically meaningful inscription-number cohorts and index concepts that are not single coordinated projects.
